title: Risotto alla Pescatora
subtitle: Venetian seafood risotto with prawns, squid, and mussels
excerpt: A Venetian seafood risotto with a mixed catch of prawns, squid, and mussels cooked in their own juices and folded through a saffron-scented risotto made with fish stock. Rich but not heavy.

recipe.sourceNotes: Risotto alla pescatora, or fisherman's risotto, is a Venetian and broader northern Italian coastal tradition. The dish uses whatever the fishing catch provides, making the exact composition variable. The key technique is separate cooking: the seafood is cooked quickly over high heat and added at the end, never long-cooked into the risotto base where it would become rubbery.

content.text: The cardinal rule of seafood risotto is not to overcook the seafood. Cook the mussels first in wine to generate the steaming liquid, use that liquid as part of the stock, and add the prawns and squid only in the last few minutes of the risotto's cooking time. No cheese goes in, cheese and seafood is not an Italian combination.

Steam open the mussels: heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan over high heat. Add the mussels and 100 ml of the wine. Cover and cook for 3 minutes until opened. Strain the juice into the hot fish stock. Remove the mussels from most of their shells, leaving a few in shell for presentation. Discard any that didn't open.

Start the risotto: heat 3 tablespoons of oil in a wide saucepan over medium heat. Cook the shallots for 5 minutes, then add half the garlic and the chilli for 2 minutes. Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until translucent. Pour in the remaining wine and stir until absorbed.

Add the hot stock a ladleful at a time, stirring frequently and waiting for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. Add the saffron water with the second ladle. Continue for 14 to 16 minutes.

In the last 5 minutes of cooking, add the squid with a ladleful of stock. In the last 3 minutes, add the prawns. When the rice is al dente and the prawns are pink, stir in the mussels and parsley. Season. Rest for 2 minutes, then serve, the risotto should flow very slightly when spooned onto a plate.
